utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. May we briefly go into private session so that I can discuss a matter of witness scheduling with the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would it be convenient to wait until this witness has finished his evidence, do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That would be fine, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good. Yes. Good afternoon to you, sir. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies, and I think Ms. Residovic still has some questions to go. Could I point out, Ms. Residovic, that one of the photographs you showed to the witness yesterday has not yet been made an exhibit. If you want it as an exhibit, you should remember to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will probably, once again, show the same photograph to the witness and then I will tender it as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. Before the break, if you remember yesterday, we spoke about part of your testimony in which you say and mention that you recognise, among the persons in your yard, Dusan Kruskarov. You responded to that, that is correct, that you recognised him by his voice?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This has been -- this has been stated in page 536 of the transcript. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now ask you, Mr. Jusufi, are you aware that Dusan Kruskarov is -- has been ill for quite a number of years, and then that since 1981 he is not engaged in any of the reserve forces of the police or of the army?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he is not sick. I see him -- he's seen everyday walking along the streets. I don't know that he's ill or sick. I know that he's working at Kekenovski. I don't know that he's sick.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness document 1D 18, number 65 ter, page 1D 0262, which presents -- which is a summary of the interview of the suspect which was made by the investigator Matti Raatikainen, where -- and I would like to point your attention to the fact that the investigator states that Kruskarovski has never been a police reserve officer; that he has been relieved from duty because of -- because of cancer; that is he not capable to work; and that in point 3, the investigator points that the credibility of Elmaz Jusufi in that sense should be reexamined. In the conclusion of point 4D, which continues at page 1D 0263 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would also ask to have that page shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- the investigator believes that this witness has not been in Ljuboten at the time of the events, and that is not true. He also states that the physical situation -- the physical condition and the condition of the illness of this person confirms this conclusion of the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask to show -- maybe we have not shown the second page. So paragraph 1 of the second page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it might be enough at this stage, Ms. Residovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- if you asked the witness whether he could make any observation on those comments.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, bearing in mind these comments, do you still stay with the fact that -- Kruskarov is healthy and that he was a reservist?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about things as they were five years ago. I don't know what the situation is like today. I only heard his voice and judged from his voice that it was him, and I heard him saying, "Put some petrol over the car." This is what I heard. It was his voice. I didn't say that I saw him -- I saw his face, but he is my neighbour and I know his voice very well. That's why I said that it was him. I -- from the voice, I can tell whoever of my neighbours he is, because we grew up together. We live side by side. Whoever of them might be, I could recognise him by the voice. That's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I would be able to conclude, Mr. Jusufi, everything that you have heard and all the persons that you eventually mentioned were recognised by the voice only, not because you saw those persons?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't see them, because they were wearing masks. So I couldn't ascertain exactly that they were them from the face, because I didn't see the face. But from the voice, yes, because they were dressed in military uniforms, the uniforms of reservists. Even before that day, I think this happened. We used to see them every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember, Mr. Jusufi, that yesterday when you were addressing the Court, which is written on a page of the transcript 529, line 8 and 9, that you have said that the door beside which your son was hit, that then you precisely said that he --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "The door touched the feet of my son because my son fell on the stomach." Do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can tell you the same thing today.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that after that, your son bleeded heavily?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that he was wearing jeans at that time, the jeans that he took on -- that he put on after waking up? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was wearing pyjamas before when he was sleeping and in a couple of seconds, he put on his jeans and went to the door, to close the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me, given that he was bleeding heavily, were all his clothes bloody, also his pants, his trousers and his T-shirt?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When blood started to come out, he was lying on the floor and then they turned him on his side. I saw him bleeding. The blood fell on the carpet. It is true. There is nothing to comment on here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And his clothes were all bloody, not only the carpet; right?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We put some -- a piece of sheet on his wound. We, ourselves. I mean, his mother. When he fell down and when the policemen came and kicked the door open, they managed to open it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The clothes he was hit and the clothes that he was bleeding in, nobody changed those clothes in your house, and that's how he was transferred or taken to the house of your daughter-in-law -- of your daughter?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the same clothes. Even when we buried him, we buried him in the same clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was also photographed in the same clothes by the local hoxha, by the local priest?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would repeat -- I would again ask that the witness is shown a photograph 65 ter 608, page 7, number 0501-6265.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw this photograph yesterday and you recognised it. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we say that at these clothes, there is just a little bit blood that has probably remained from the blanket he was lying on? There is no visible blood on the other parts of the clothes. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he was lying down, the blood fell on the -- on the carpet, and his mother was standing beside him and cleaning the blood. She tried to tie up the wound, and all his blood came out. We do not dress up a dead person. You should be certain that this is how it was. I saw him with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Tell me, your wife at the very moment when your son was in the corridor, she tried to stop the bleeding or did you previously take him to the -- did you previously take him to the room?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First she tried to stop the bleeding, to clean the blood that came out, and then when the blood stopped, she took him -- she took him and put him on the couch. She kept cleaning his blood all the time, hoping that the bleeding would stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask that the witness is shown the exhibit of the Prosecutor, P4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, these photographs were shown to you by the learned colleague the Prosecutor during his examination.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask the question to you, please tell me: Your wife was completely conscious all the time and she allowed it --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. My colleague has gotten up. Maybe he would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Apologies for the interruption. I showed the witness a photograph that was marked as P9, and I believe we're looking at a different photograph. If it's P4, we're looking at a different photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it is a mistake, but P4 was -- we wrote that this is P4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: P4 is the photograph that was at tab 1 of the bundle that was shown to Mrs. Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mm-hm, I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, I apologise. This photograph has not been shown to you but to your wife. Tell me, do you recognise this photograph and the person that is on it?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, of course. It's Rami Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that your wife immediately went to clean the blood of your son. Your wife was conscious and did everything to assist your son. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She was very upset, but she believed and I believed, too, that he was not yet dead. We thought that he was just wounded. And she tried to administer some help to him. And then after that, she lost consciousness when she saw him die, because she has a weak heart. She cannot stand blood.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you well, your wife fell -- fainted after she saw your son being dead. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. She fainted. I was on -- optimistic until that moment, hoping against hope that he would live. But then we never thought that he would die so quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, on the front page, you can see that these trousers are not bloody, could you -- can you?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it. But when my wife was cleaning up his wound, his blood, probably she has pushed down a little bit his trousers. I don't see any problems in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these trousers are not buttoned-up, really?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't have time enough to button-up his trousers because it was a matter of seconds, before he changed into his trousers. He was in pyjamas first, and when he saw the blast -- he heard the blast and the door -- all the house shook. Then he just put on his trousers and didn't have time to button-up trousers, and then he rushed to the door. It was -- it took only 10 seconds, all this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can take these photographs away. I would now ask Your Honours to show photograph 65 ter -- I didn't get the number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could you like to -- for her to repeat the number, please? The interpreter didn't get the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter number 608, page 7, photograph number 0501-6265, that the witness recognised and described, to tender it as an evidence of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe the witness has looked at two photographs that are not exhibits. One is presently on the screen; the other appeared to be the photograph that is also at tab 2 of the bundle used with Mrs. Jusufi. Now, are you tendering both photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. But I thought that the one that is now displayed on the screen is already Exhibit P4. If I'm wrong, then I would like to tender this photograph as an exhibit of the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, you are correct, Ms. Residovic. So the one that is at tab 2, ID 0482T will now be received as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You take all this picture from my side, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take the photograph away from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, I will now ask you something completely different. You know Kenan Salievski or Kenan Saliu. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a villager of our village. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time of the event, in August 2001, he was a president of the village, in Ljuboten, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chairman of the -- of a staff, a Crisis Staff, because all villages had their own Crisis Staffs. They were at the school. This is what I know about him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He is today also the president of the local community, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, in any event, he is a very important and influential person in the village?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time of the event, as a president of a Crisis Staff, will you agree with me that he knew well the situation in the village?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation was calm and quiet in the village at that time. We had a normal life, until the 11th. Nothing happened. There were some shots, but life was normal for us, like, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, we know and you have said it as well, that at that time you were also ill and that your movement was limited, given the situation of your health. Will you agree with me that you received many of the information by hearing them from other persons and not seeing them firsthand or that you were present at those events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We talked all the time about developments, things. People came and visited me, had coffee, we discussed how things were. Nothing extraordinary was happening. Had we known what was going to happen, we would have left a month ago. But until the last day, we didn't know anything. We didn't expect this to happen. If we did, of course we would have left the village six months ago. But nothing was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So you learned about the things from the village when your relatives and neighbours were coming at your house and were talking about it, but you did not go personally at the meetings or you didn't go around the village personally to -- to find out what is going on in the village. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. But I was eager to know what was going on. I wanted to leave if we had known that, but we didn't know that this was going to happen to us. I always kept in touch with people because my house was near the check-point, and they said to us, "Stay quiet, stay there, nothing is going to happen."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours for the sake of the record, document 65 ter 608, page 7, bearing ERN number 0501-6265 will become Exhibit 1D 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Kenan Salievski is a president of a Crisis -- of the Crisis Staff. He was present at the meetings that were held in the village, and he personally talked with certain people, and you can agree with me that his knowledge of what really was going on in the village was better than yours?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if this witness can speak to the knowledge of another person in the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we can understand the question well enough, Mr. Saxon, to be an inquiry whether this witness would accept that the chairman of the crisis committee should have a better knowledge of what was happening in the village than he. That is the way The Chamber would understand it, and I think that is what was intended.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you answer it, Mr. Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Salievski, as a president of the Crisis Staff, would certainly have information much more precise than those in your possession?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course, I didn't have as much information as Kenan had because I did not attend those meetings, but I heard information about the situation, that the situation was calm, that nothing was going on. Compared to him, I would say I knew only 1 per cent of the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me, Mr. Jusufi, if I were to tell you that from your village, the NLA members were Suat Salu, Riza Jonuzi, Besim Murtezani, Rafet Bajrami, Shefket Bajrami, Fikret Aliu, Rushan Jashari, Ramadan Alimi, Musa Selimi, Refedin Selimi, Faik Murati, Shefket Murati, Zeqir Murati, Rasim Murati, and probably other persons that I would not mention this time. Do you agree with me, that these people were NLA members or affiliated with it?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. I cannot provide you with any answer because I did not hear about these things. I regret, but I really cannot give you any answer to this question, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Jusufi, you would -- if those facts were correct, the president of the Crisis Staff would learn about it?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. You should ask him about these things because I have nothing to do with this matter. I have no knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You are familiar with the name Baki Halimi?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is from the village. I now him. A co-villager. Not related to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are also aware that he was known in the village by the name Commander Lisi?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. This is the first time I hear about Lisi. I have no idea about this name.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were now, Mr. Jusufi, to tell you that Baki Halimi, on the Saturday of 11th of August, 2001, convened a meeting of all males who could defend the village, to a meeting, you could confirm this fact as correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. To what I heard, not that I saw anything with my own eyes, but I heard that Baki Halimi was at the check-point in a camp. Maybe it was not a camp, but it was a camp surrounded by policemen. Not only Baki, but perhaps 2.000 other people who were there on that check-point surrounded by the police. I don't know about this meeting, and I don't think that this meeting was convened. He is nothing. He is only a teacher in the primary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the information that he was on the check-point, are you referring to the Sunday, the 12th?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I refer to the Sunday. As for the Saturday, I have no knowledge. I apologise once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm, Mr. Jusufi, that your sons, Rami and Salahedin, together with Fatmir and Meshir Kamberi, Avni Hyseni and others were in the meeting with the Commander Lisi on the Saturday evening?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, on Saturday, my son was not there, not on the Friday, not on the 15th, not on the 8th, not on the 7th. He had handymen working on that facility that you have seen on the picture. He was busy -- busy with these handymen. He was in the house. As for the others that you mentioned, I don't know about them, whether they were or not. But for my son, I can tell you that he was not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, could you confirm that, because of that situation where the checkpoints were organised in the village that -- because of that situation on the Saturday evening, your daughter-in-law and your grandchildren went to your daughter's, to the Durmisina neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want me to explain about this or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. I just wanted to ask you that?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me that actually at that moment you were not aware what the -- some members of NLA had on the previous date, on the 10th of August gone into the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I not only didn't see this, but I didn't even hear about this. I never heard that there were NLA in Ljuboten village. And you should know this for a fact. I'm stating this publicly that there was no NLA persons in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think that there is a slight problem in the transcript in the lines 14 to 18. You have asked whether you wish -- whether you wished to explain something. In the line 17, I said that I did not wish you to explain and that I only wanted to ask you this, but later in the line 18, there is your answer "No." So in order to avoid the contradiction of what your reply actually was, I would like to repeat the previous question, and that is the question whether you can confirm that because of the situation in the village, your daughter-in-law and your grandchildren went to your daughter's, to the Durmisina neighbourhood. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand correctly the neighbourhood that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the house of your daughter?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They all went. My daughter-in-law and the children, they all went to my daughter's place, because the children were scared. They were very scared of the police because the police was just nearby. The church was near our house. They were all in panic, and I told them to do so. I even told my late son to join them and to leave, but he didn't want to leave me and his mother alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. We have now clarified it, and we avoided a contradiction. It appeared as you have said that your daughter-in-law and grandchildren had not gone, but I think that everything is now clear in the transcript. I would go back to what I have asked you before this clarification. On the 10th of August, 2001, you have learned that at the Ljubotenski Bachila locality from a mine explosion, eight soldiers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia were killed and many soldiers were wounded. Have you learned this on the 10th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about this. I heard that the mine explosion killed eight or -- I don't know exactly how many they were, but I heard about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And all the time after that, you were inside your house, and except with your family, you never discussed that event. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know at all whether any of the persons who have placed the mine were from the village of Ljuboten, and you don't know whether some persons who have placed the mine there on that date came into Ljuboten village to hide. You never received any information on that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no knowledge about this. I have no comment about this, because I didn't hear or see anything related to this matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at the end - just a few more questions, Mr. Jusufi - you stated that your daughter-in-law and grandchildren went to your daughter's. If I were to tell you that your sons Rami and Salahedin took also your wife to the house of your daughters's on the Saturday evening, that would be the complete truth. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Saturday evening? Can you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So on the Saturday, 11th of August, your sons have taken your wife to the house of your daughter's and also tried to make you go, but you refused; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. My wife did not go. The younger son went there with all the children. The seven children, the younger son and the two daughters-in-law, they went to my daughter's, while myself and my wife and the other son remained at home. This is the truth. I said to him, "You go, too," but he didn't want to leave his mother and me alone in the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On Saturday evening, is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that your sons returned to convince you that you should go to your daughter's, but that you did not want that and that you remained with them in the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained in the house. Three persons remained in the house: myself, my wife and my son. Nobody else. The others left for my daughter's.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jusufi, for answering all questions that I have asked you, and I regret if you suffered some additional inconveniences because of your health status in relation to my questioning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. I would like to ask questions to the witness. I hope that I will avoid my questions overlapping with the questions with my colleague, Edina Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jusufi, first I regret the loss of your son. I know that it is difficult for you to answer regarding these difficult moments, but you have to understand that I need to ask you several questions related to the event. Can I start asking my questions, Mr. Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You say that you received disability pension; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the state, the Republic of Macedonia, is paying your pension? Is that --

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It means that you're using free of charge your health insurance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm insured because I worked 40 years for the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the village of Ljuboten, the teaching is in the Albanian language in the primary school?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your children and your grandchildren are educated free of charge in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that in the Republic of Macedonia, every four years there are elections?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that in Macedonia there are parliamentary, residential, and local elections?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jusufi, that in all elections the Albanians vote freely and on a mass scale?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they did cast their votes. Some did, some didn't, just like in other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Albanians come out and vote freely?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, yes, they vote freely. Who wants to vote goes out and votes; who doesn't, didn't. I did cast my vote, although I am an invalid.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do the Albanians in Macedonia have their representatives in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that in the village of Ljuboten, the Albanians freely go and vote?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, freely. There was never any incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your late son, Rami Jusufi, has served in the army?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Slovenia, in Crnomelj.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was -- what branch was he serving his conscription in?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quartermasters. I don't know what exactly this means, but it was equal to master unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Whether in the period between the 10th and 12th of August, you had running water in your house?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. During the summer, we don't have water. Not only in August, even now we don't have water during the summer. And we -- during this particular year, we used to carry water on our tractors from Bashinec.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you store the water inside your house once you would take it?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you would take the water home from Bashinec, did you leave the containers where you would take the water inside the house?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would fill plastic bottles, 100 or 200 bottles, and that would last for ten days or two weeks. Even nowadays we do the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you store these plastic bottles inside your home?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the house, we keep the bottles in sacks, and then we take the sacks on the tractors and fill the bottles with water.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have a telephone line in your home?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have a telephone line in the period between the 10th and the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until 8.00 on the 12th of August, I did. But when the electricity went off, the phone was not working, because it works on electricity. So as soon as the electricity went off, the phone was no longer working.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that your telephone is connected to an electric outlet? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you clarify the model of the telephone -- the make of the telephone that you have at home?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. That phone is no longer working. The police destroyed it with the bursts of fire directed at the house. The phone was completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Whether in the period between the 10th and the 12th of August you were using a mobile phone?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Personally, I didn't. This land line, I use it very rarely, only to speak to my relatives. And, as I said, it worked at nearly 8.00 on the 12th of August. But as for mobile phones, I didn't have one and neither did my son. Nobody of us had a mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you clarify whether it was 8.00 in the morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. To which date do you refer?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You have previously replied that the question [sic] was not working from 8.00 on the 12th of August. Is that 8.00?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 8.00 a.m. As soon as the electricity went off, the phone was no longer in working order.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 10th of August, 2001, that is the Friday, you have seen how grenades, shells were falling on to the village for the entire day?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This I have seen with my own eyes. And I saw when the shell fell near the mosque, in the direction of the mosque, and in the direction of the graveyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you indicate the number of that shells?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw and heard two, because I was out in the yard when it exploded and when smoke came out. I heard the blast.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher show the panorama of the village of Ljuboten, ERN NOO5-7605. I apologise, 005-7605.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Dash, not slash.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we enlarge this photograph? Could the witness indicate the locations where he has seen the shells falling? We are referring to Friday, the 10th. I would like to ask the usher to give him ...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to mark the places where you have seen the shells falling on the Friday morning, the 10th -- 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the morning. It wasn't in the morning. Not in the morning. It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It means that you will now mark the locations where the shells were falling on the Friday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here at the mosque, on the left minaret, then it fell near the door of the neighbour. The other one fell at the graves, but I can't seem to found out where the graveyard is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, Mr. Jusufi, to mark them with the marker that you have in your hand.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can't find the cemetery here; this is my problem. This is where I saw it fall. I can't find the graveyard here. This is where I saw the smoke rising from the graveyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you at least mark what you see?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mosque, yes, I can -- I can mark. Shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mark it with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The place that you marked with number 1, was that the place that you saw the shell falling; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I can't find the graveyard yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark it number 2?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot mark it because I cannot find it, where it is. I cannot find the graveyard, so I cannot mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in, into the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour. Perhaps to assist because the zooming-in motion is actually done on the screen in front of the witness, and the witness is looking at the photograph on the ELMO. Perhaps if the witness could be directed to look at the computer screen, he may be able to assist more.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please look in the computer desk where you will be able to see the photograph zoomed-in?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can't find the graveyard. So it may be about 50 metres in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Then if you can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I propose to have this picture marked as -- with number 1, to have it tendered in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D 1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said you had been working in a state company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked in the Institute of Agriculture. We were together with the Faculty of Agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You also said that the Ljuboten residents are engaged in agricultural works; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I would say 90 per cent of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that your family was engaged in agricultural works as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What kind of agricultural works your family is engaged in?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I grow tobacco, watermelon and melon, vegetables. Wheat and corn.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your son, Rami Jusufi, on Friday, 10th of August, 2001, was in Skopje and he was selling watermelons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your statement, Mr. Jusufi, of October 3, 2004, 2D 28, page 4, paragraph 17, in the English version, you say that in the last two days before the event, your son was doing some construction work in the house and that he was doing it also on the Friday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Friday, he sold watermelon, also on Saturday. On the 8th and 9th, he had some handyman who were working to finish a stable, is the correct version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could I state, Mr. Jusufi, that these two statements regarding what your son was doing on Friday differ from one another?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they do not differ. On Friday, he sold melon; on Saturday did the same. I don't think there is any difference in there. I saw it in my own eyes and I was there. Why are you trying to put this to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I just read out the statement that you have given before the ICTY OTP investigators that you gave on October 3, 2004. 2D 28, page 4, paragraph 17, whereby you say that: "In the last two days before the event, my son was doing some construction works in the house. He was also doing it on the Friday." That is your statement?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that is wrong. It is a mistake. Maybe the translator has got it wrong. He worked with it on the 7th, with the other handyman on the 8th, then the -- then the construction materials ran out and they stopped that. And then he had to sell the melons, and he went to sell it, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When did you go to bed on the Friday evening, on August 10th, 2001.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As usual, when we felt like sleeping, we went to bed. We watched television for a while. Maybe it was 10.00, or 9.00. It's a long day and the short night. So people go to sleep earlier than usual. They don't even watch television a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you locked your gate on the Friday evening?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We closed the gate always. We do it now, we did it 20 years ago. We never leave the door open, or the gate open.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When did you wake up on Saturday, August 11, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I tell you? It depends. My sleep varies, but usually I wake up at 4.00 in the morning, because I have pills to sleep. I have a bad sleep. People who work all day, usually they sleep late in the morning, until 8.00 or so. But my wife and myself, we usually wake up earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your son on Saturday was in Skopje and returned home at 1900 hours?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not at 7.00, a little bit later. I can't be very precise, but I remember that it was before night fell. It was still light when he came from selling the watermelon. The police recognised him at the check-point and let -- they let him go before the others. Please, this is what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that you confirm -- does it mean that you confirm to me that your son returned home on Saturday and then at that time it was still visible; it was still daylight outside?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was getting darker. I was at the gate. It was still daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that on Saturday your son, Rami Jusufi, was not doing any construction works in his yard?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. He wasn't doing any construction work.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your statement dated October 3, 2004, 2D 28, page 4, paragraph 17, you say that the last two days before the event, your son was doing some construction works around the house; that he did it also on the Friday. He was home the entire day Saturday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Neither on Saturday nor on Friday. I told you. Why do you ask me again? Friday and Saturday, he sold watermelon. He wasn't a handyman. He left his car there and helped them in one way or another, told them what to do for an hour or so, or half an hour, or a quarter of an hour, but this doesn't mean that he was a handyman. You may say as you wish, but this is not exactly how it was. Is it correct, that on Saturday it was raining and it was -- and there were thunderstorms, that many shells were thrown on the village and that I was able to hear light fire-arms shooting. I could see the places, from my garden, where the shells hit and even later it started dawning. When dawn came, there was raining and there was lightening. But I don't know when it -- where it fell. When you see the light of the lightening and hear the sound, at that moment the shell fell, and it resembled the noise of the lightening. It was very interesting to note that, but I can't tell you where it fell. The sounds were synchronised.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it true that the village was shelled with many shells?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many shells were thrown, but I don't know where they fell. I could hear the roar of shells, but I don't know where they fell. I can't tell you how many there were, because a tank was close by. Maybe one kilometre away or less -- one kilometre and a half. The tank was buried in the ground and there was a police check-point 200 metres away, that I saw it with my own eyes. I can show you even now, if you want, where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was the tank, that you now mention, close to your house?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not close. When I went out in the yard, I could see it. The barrel was directed to the village. The tank was there on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In respect what you said, that many shells hit the village, could you tell me whether there were more than 20 or less than 20?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to lie. I don't want to give a false number. It's better if we leave it at that, without putting a number. I can't give you an accurate number.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that you were not able to see from your yard where exactly the shells hit?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I saw some fall at the mosque and near the graveyard because I saw the smoke rising up. For the others, I don't know. I know that a house was burned because of the shelling. It was down in the Reka. They showed this to me, and once when I passed by with the car, I saw it with my own eyes. You can ask those who have done it. Maybe they can give you the right number.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, should I continue my examination, because we are getting close to the break time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if it would be convenient to you, Mr. Apostolski, we can break now and we will resume at 10 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, I will continue with several more questions. A while ago, you told me that you saw when the shells were falling during the day-time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that a house was burned down in Reka?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that a -- some neighbourhood in Ljuboten that is called Reka?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's called Reka, but it is far from our neighbourhood. It did not burn that area, but the shell only fell there and I saw this with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can I state that due to the shelling on Saturday, 11th of August, 2001, several houses were burning in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Saturday, no. As far as I know, only that shell. Nuredin Ismaili, I know that the shell fell on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: A while ago, you said that several shells fell -- that many shells fell on the Saturday?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did fall, but I don't know where, in which locations, because it was raining and I was not able to see all of them. I was not outside. I only heard the noise of the explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That means that you can only confirm that several shells fell on Saturday, 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can only confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that together inside the house on the 10th and 11th of August your wife, your son, your daughter-in-law and their children, their four children lived?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that correct, that in the house adjacent to yours, your younger son Salahedin lives together with his family?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your younger son, Salahedin, on Saturday night took the children in the and have transferred them to your daughter's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was it possible for them to go to the house of your daughter without the knowledge of your wife?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all there in the house, myself included, when Rami and Salahedin's children and wives went. We were all together. We were discussing what to do, and I told them to go to my daughter's. My oldest son said no, I will not go, I cannot leave you and my mother alone, while the rest, they went to my daughter's place because her house is in a sort of a valley. So the children and the daughters-in-law left and went to my daughter's place, and this happened after dark fell. Now whether it was 9.00 or 9.30, that I don't know, but I know that all of them left and only the three of us remained in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that your wife was present when they left; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, your wife has stated before this Honourable Court on the 7th of May at page 76, lines 12 and 15, that your son Salahedin was in his house on Saturday evening. That is in contradiction to the statement that you are now giving. Could you tell me what is the truth?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is what I'm telling you. As for what my wife said, I don't know. She tends to forget. I know that we were all gathered together, and I told them to leave. My wife has heart problems, and maybe she was uncomfortable here in the courtroom when testifying, so I don't know what she told you, but what I'm telling you is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree anyway with me, Mr. Elmaz, that your statement and the statement -- the statement of your wife are different?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it's different, and I don't think that this really matters. Her house is about 20 metres far from our house. I don't know how my wife explained all this, but I don't see it relevant. What I'm telling you is correct, because if that was the case, he would stay in my house, but I guess my wife was kind of lost when she said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did any other persons come in your house on the evening on Saturday, 11th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You know why? Because I would have been able to see that. You should know that on that night, I couldn't sleep at all, and if someone was there, I would have heard that. Even if someone is at the gate, I would have heard that. I hear very well. I guarantee that nobody was there because we lock the entrance door before we go to sleep. I don't know at what time we went to bed. I did go to bed, but I didn't fell asleep immediately. I heard noises of vehicles because you can hear them passing by the street near our house. I don't know in which direction they went. As I said, I need pills because otherwise I can't sleep well. This is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that if some persons were present in the yard, you would have surely heard them talking about the evening, the night between 11th and 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could hear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the Saturday evening, your son and your wife went to bed immediately after 12.00?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean 12.00, at midnight? I didn't understand your question. Can you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: We are talking about 2400 hours.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see, 2400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I thought 2400 hours.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that we went to bed. There are three beds in that room. We all went to bed. They did sleep, but I personally couldn't sleep because I cannot go to sleep without taking the pills previously. But even if you take pills, when you hear noise you cannot go to sleep, and I could hear the noise coming from the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: May I state that your wife and your son Rami were asleep at 2400 hours?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wasn't asleep, but they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your wife, in her statement given on 22nd of April, 2007, 2D 2253, page 2, paragraph 3, line 3, is saying that: "We did not go to bed that night. We were frightened." And this statement of your wife is in contradiction to the one that you are giving now. Could you clarify what is the -- what is true?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Can you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You confirmed that your wife and your son at 2400 hours were asleep; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your wife, in the statement given on the 22nd of April, 2007, 2D 2253, page 2, paragraph 3, line 3, states: "We could not sleep that night. We were frightened." Can I conclude that they are two completely different statements; yours given presently and hers given on the 22nd of April?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe she couldn't sleep that night, too. She was sleeping in a separate bed. Now, I don't know whether she could go to sleep or not, but she was lying down in a separate bed. My son was, I guess, asleep because he was tired. And as for my wife, maybe she couldn't go to sleep, too. She doesn't sleep that long usually, and I don't see any major difference here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the Saturday evening, your gate was locked?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that on Sunday, on the 12th of August, you got up at 5.00 or 6.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whether it was 5.00 or 6.00, I don't know exactly. But as I have stated earlier, I usually wake up at 4.00 and stay awake and like that. Anyways, it was between 5.00 and 6.00 that I woke up. I had something to eat. My wife usually wakes up around the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your wife took you to the yard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can go by myself, but there is an elevated part, so she needs to push me a little bit, but at that time I was in a better health state than I am now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It means that your wife left you in the yard and immediately went into the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. She went inside, she went to the garden, she looked after her own work, she cleaned and washed. She did the usual female business. I was near the car, near the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that your wife, apart from the work in the garden, did not do any other tasks in your yard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know how it is in villages. There is a lot of work to be done. Women have a lot of work to do. She might have been cleaning or washing something. I can't tell you exactly what she was doing and what particular time, but she works all the time. She cleans the yard, washes the yard, does her usual chores.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You remained in the yard, you did not go outside of the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I remained in the yard. It was a little bit cooler. I usually stay in the yard when it's hot, but I think I went in before 8.00. I didn't look at the watch. And, to tell you the truth, it did not occur to me at that time that this would befell on us. Had it occurred to me, I would have done something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that from the yard, when your wife took you there, you did not leave it to go on the street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained there, and I could move then on my own because that's the way how that location is. When you go up, she helps me, but then when I go down, I can come back myself. I'm used to that area because I have been like this for ten years. I'm surprised with your questions. Every invalid knows how to operate --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did your wife help you go out from the yard to the street?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go out on the street. I was inside my yard. The street is on the other side of the gate. This is not a street; this is a yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that you have heard a loud sound, and this is how the gate opened; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened when I was inside the house, in the corridor, when I already returned to the house. Your questions are not being asked in order. I called Muzafer on my way back because he's a neighbour. I said to him, "Come, let's have a coffee together." We entered the house. We were in the corridor. My son was sleeping in the room. This was before 8.00, maybe quarter to 8.00. As I said, I did not look at the watch, but the electricity went off at 8.00. We were having coffee, and a normal conversation like any other day, as if nothing was going on. Now you're asking me about the moment when the door exploded, and I'll tell you before the Honourable Judges that this explosion was a loud one. The sound was similar to the sound of shelling, and the windows, both in the ground floor and upper floor, were shaking. At that moment, his mother, my son's mother, called on her son, said to him, "Wake up, son, the door has exploded." And in that moment, he put on his clothes, hurriedly. You asked me previously why he did not button up his trousers. He didn't have time to do that because the gate is only 4 metres away from the entrance door. The room where my son was sleeping, if you consider the distance of the corridor, which is 2 metres, and 1 metre from the house, so it's 4 or 5 metres altogether. So when they entered the yard, they fired shots in the air. They did not fire in the direction of the entrance door, the door that takes you inside the corridor, but they were opposite there. I was just on the doorstep of -- of the room, and I said to him, to my son, "Don't." And he said, "I just close the door." So he went to the door and he was opposite to them, and they immediately fired a burst of fire. I guess the bullets caught him immediately, and he fell on the ground immediately. He was only 1 metre away from me when he fell down, on my right side. Maybe you don't know here, but Macedonians know very well the type of doors I'm talking about. These are Slovenian-make doors. He fell immediately on the ground, and he just uttered the words, "They killed me." At the moment, they fired in the corridor. It was similar to hail. These bullets resembled a hail. The corridor is about 7 metres long. The phone was on one side, and the gas container was near it -- the washing machine. They came there at the door, the police, and the policemen kicked the door open very strongly. I thought that the door was going do fall on me because it is quite a tall door.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jusufi.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have more to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that until the explosion -- does it mean that until the explosion, the gate of the door was not open?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No. The outside door, the gate, was opened when it exploded. They destroyed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I am asking you, Mr. Jusufi, is it that until the explosion the gate to the door was closed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be a problem of the translation, Mr. Apostolski. But the question as it is translated into English is confusing. Are you speaking of the gate from the street to the yard?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Or the door from the yard into the house?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Translate. [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm referring throughout about the gate to the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. So your question is concerning whether that was locked at the time of the explosion -- effects to that gate?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my question is whether that gate, up until the moment of the explosion, was closed. I didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, the gate was closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your statement, Mr. Jusufi, of the 9th of February, 2003, 2D 12, page 4, paragraph 1, line 1, you are saying that you have heard five APCs and five covered trucks, while in the addendums or corrections to the statement of Elmaz Jusufi, according to Rule 92 ter, 2D 2295, page 3, paragraph 6, line 3, you are saying: "I have seen one APC and one covered truck." And yesterday, before this Tribunal, you have stated that you didn't know what the number was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see them, but I did not give any number, whether there were two, three or five. It is a fact that I saw both trucks and the other, whatever you call it, pass by, but I did not give any number. Several passed by. They entered the yard of the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the photograph 65 ter -- excuse me, can we see the photograph 65 ter 199.3? If the usher could show this photograph to the witness so that he could mark it. Could we zoom out the photo so that the entire yard is visible? Could we zoom it out? A bit further so that the door to the right is visible. A bit more, a bit more. A slight bit more. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark with 1 where were you standing when you have seen the vehicles, regardless of whether there were five, one, or whatever the number?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the tap.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Please mark the -- show on the picture?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was here. I was here. Here is the water tap and the hose.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Please number?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If you could mark it with the number 1. Number 1. Could you confirm that where the number 1 is, you were located on the Sunday morning, when you have seen the covered trucks and the transporters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was staying here at that moment, but you should know that I am not fixed in one place. I move about. It's a big yard. But from here, you can see better and people from the street can also see me when I'm here, but we're talking about big vehicles. And you can see these big vehicles even if you're 10 metres far away from them. I cannot stay for two hours in one single place. I move about.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "Carriers" instead of "transporters."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you have seen the vehicles, was the door looking to the street closed?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was closed. The gate was closed. But don't look at this gate as it is now because I've lifted them up with some concrete. In the past, they were not this tall. We could see them even better. The concrete layer you're seeing now is new. When the door was -- the gate was burnt down, the concrete was destroyed as well. The picture you're seeing is the picture of the gate as it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What was the colour of the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know the colour of the hermelines.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I don't know the colour of the hermeline. I have never seen one.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may not know it, but I do know it, because I have seen them pass by on several occasions. I cannot tell you the exact colour, but the hermelines are in one plain colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me what was the colour of the truck?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was of a military colour, at least it resembled to me to be a military colour. But I did not pay much attention to the colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please could I tender this photograph as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D 2, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown now a photograph, Exhibit 1D 2? Could I ask the kind assistance of the usher to show it to the witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, do you see the photograph in front of you, first of all?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this wall -- at this wall on the 12th of August, 2001, where -- where they are in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark the door with the number 1? In the picture below. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And mark the wall with the number 2.

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you write the number 2 again? It's not -- okay, then there is no need. Okay. Could you confirm now that the number 1 was used to mark your door that was there on the 12th of August, 2001, and that the number 2 marks the wall?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you confirm that a while ago when you were speaking, you were actually speaking about this door, that this was the door that was closed?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask that this photograph is received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D 3, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On the Sunday morning, on the 12th of August, 2001, in your house there were you, your wife, your son Rami, and your relative Muzafer there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did Imret Jusufi come to your house at all on that morning?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was -- he's young. It was only the four of us in the house that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you can confirm that Imret Jusufi was at no moment inside your house on the Sunday morning?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not in the house. He was in his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the addendum to your statement of the 9th of February, 2003, on the 11th of August, 2006, 2D 60, you stated that: "Imret Jusufi came to our house somewhere around 7.00 in the morning. He brought me cigarettes and he left immediately."

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "Muzafer Jusufi came around 7.00 in the morning, after we invited him to come and have breakfast with us." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I invited him to have a coffee with me. He is -- he lives nearby. I asked him to come and join me for a coffee just as we usually do every morning. I either go to his place or he comes over to our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufi, are you familiar with the name of Sabit Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sabit Jusufi is a relative of mine, but he doesn't live near my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is he the father of Imret Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Sabit Jusufi, in the statement he has given on the 28th of September, 2004, 2D 71, page 2, paragraph 6, says: "I don't remember many important details from within those two days. I was home alone because my son Imret was in the house of Elmaz Jusufi."

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. Maybe he was in the other house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: These are two -- these are two different statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this statement of his. Maybe he was in the other house staying there out of fear. Of course, everybody was frightened. Everybody was hiding. Now, whether he was in another house or in his own house, that I don't know. But he was young and, of course, he was hiding. I cannot tell you any more than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Xhevdet Jusufovski?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's a relative of mine. His shop was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you may allow to go to a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that when you woke up on the Sunday and when your wife took you to the yard, you were by yourself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that when you woke up on the Sunday, your -- and your wife took you to the yard, you were by yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were alone in the yard, myself and my wife. My son was asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Before this Honourable Tribunal you testified today that if there was -- there was someone in the yard on Saturday evening towards the Sunday and the Sunday morning, you -- you would have surely heard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Because I was outside the whole time. Whoever was there, I was able to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that you have not heard of the name of Commander Lisi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with this name. I haven't heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Komandant Miskoja?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said yesterday that beside your house, there is the house of Fatmir Kamberi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Fatmir Kamberi's house -- actually, he has two houses; a new house that he has built, but he does not live there. Fatmir's house is next to Sande's house, the neighbours here know that. It is next to Sande's house. It is true that his house is there, but he doesn't live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see Fatmir Kamberi in the weekend between 10th and 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see him very often, maybe once a year, because we are not closely related. We're kind of distant relatives. Maybe I see him only once or twice a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is that correct that your son and Fatmir Kamberi are friends?

utterances.speaker: ELMAZ JUSUFI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A neighbour is a neighbour. You cannot call a neighbour a friend. Fatmir was a neighbour, like the other neighbours. You cannot call him a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
